foods-01.meaning: Makan siang denotes the midday meal and can also refer to the act of eating it.
foods-01.common_use: Widely understood and used in contemporary Indonesia.
foods-01.preferred: Makan siang is the normal everyday choice for lunch.
foods-01.region: National Indonesian usage; no specific regional limit identified.

claims.proposition: Makan siang refers to a meal eaten around midday.
Makan siang is the normal everyday Indonesian expression for lunch.

source_leads.exact_claim: A contemporary Indonesian meal plan uses Makan Siang as its heading for the midday meal.

foods-02.meaning: Sendok is a spoon used to scoop or eat food; the word also appears in names of measuring utensils.
foods-02.common_use: Widely understood and used in contemporary Indonesia.
foods-02.preferred: Sendok is the normal everyday choice for spoon.
foods-02.region: National Indonesian usage; no specific regional limit identified.

claims.proposition: Sendok names the utensil used to scoop and eat food.
Sendok is the normal everyday Indonesian choice for spoon.

source_leads.exact_claim: The dictionary entry is a lead for the utensil meaning of sendok.
Indonesian food guidance uses sendok makan in an ordinary food-preparation context.

foods-03.meaning: Piring is a plate or shallow dish used to hold food for eating.
foods-03.common_use: Widely understood and used in contemporary Indonesia.
foods-03.preferred: Piring is the normal everyday choice for an eating plate.
foods-03.region: National Indonesian usage; no specific regional limit identified.

claims.proposition: Piring names a shallow dish on which food is served for eating.
Piring is the normal everyday Indonesian choice for an eating plate.

source_leads.exact_claim: The dictionary entry defines piring as a shallow vessel for food.
A contemporary Indonesian meal plan uses piring to describe portions of a meal.

foods-04.meaning: Enak describes food that tastes pleasant. It also has broader uses for pleasant or comfortable experiences.
foods-04.common_use: Very common and readily understood in contemporary Indonesia.
foods-04.preferred: Enak is the natural everyday choice for tasty food.
foods-04.register: Neutral and conversational; suitable beyond informal speech.
foods-04.region: National Indonesian usage; no specific regional limit identified.

claims.proposition: Enak can describe food with a pleasant taste.
Enak is a natural everyday Indonesian choice for tasty food.

source_leads.exact_claim: The dictionary entry is a lead for the taste sense and broader senses of enak.
A contemporary Indonesian government article uses makanan enak to describe appealing food.

foods-05.meaning: Saus denotes a liquid or thick sauce served with food. It covers many sauces but does not replace specific names such as sambal or kecap when those are intended.
foods-05.common_use: Common and readily understood in contemporary Indonesia, especially in names such as saus tomat and saus sambal.
foods-05.preferred: Saus is the normal general Indonesian choice for sauce; a specific condiment name is preferable when its identity matters.
foods-05.region: National Indonesian usage; no specific regional limit identified.

claims.proposition: Saus can name a liquid or thick preparation served with food.
Saus is the normal general Indonesian choice for sauce, while particular sauces often have more specific names.

source_leads.exact_claim: The dictionary entry is a lead for the food-related meaning of saus.
A contemporary Indonesian food-agency article uses saus as a food-product category.

foods-06.meaning: Biskuit denotes a small, dry baked snack. Its boundary with some kinds of kue kering depends on the product.
foods-06.common_use: Common and readily understood in contemporary Indonesia.
foods-06.preferred: Biskuit is the normal general choice for biscuit in this sense.
foods-06.region: National Indonesian usage; no specific regional limit identified.

claims.proposition: Biskuit can name a small, dry baked snack.
Biskuit is a normal everyday Indonesian choice for biscuit in this sense.

source_leads.exact_claim: The dictionary entry is a lead for the food meaning of biskuit.
A contemporary Indonesian food-agency article uses biskuit as a familiar packaged-food category.

foods-07.meaning: Nasi means rice that has been cooked for eating. Uncooked rice is usually beras; rice as a growing plant is padi.
foods-07.common_use: Extremely common and readily understood in contemporary Indonesia.
foods-07.preferred: Nasi is the normal everyday choice when rice means the cooked food.
foods-07.region: National Indonesian usage; the same form is also used in Malay.

claims.proposition: Nasi refers to rice that has been cooked for eating.
Nasi is the normal everyday Indonesian choice for cooked rice.

source_leads.exact_claim: The dictionary entry defines nasi as cooked rice.
A contemporary Indonesian meal plan uses nasi for the cooked rice served on a plate.
